test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 21 March, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

But what of the young people __whom are part of the cricket crowds, some of who are presumably born in England?__

options.text: who are part of the cricket crowds, some of who are presumably born in England
whom are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England
who are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In English,** "who"** is used as the subject of a verb, while **"whom"** is used as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• In the sentence, **"who" **is the** correct pronoun** to use after** "people"** as it is the subject of the verb "are."
 
• In the second part of the sentence,** "whom**" is the correct pronoun because it is the object of the preposition **"of."**

Therefore, the **correct sentence **would be:* "But what of the young people who are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England?"*
